title: Intentions reflection
subject: Islamic Studies
source: Seeded from islamic-studies/y8 lesson 28 (Pupil PDF worksheet: intentions reflection)
intro: Lesson 28: Sincerity (ikhlas). To understand what ikhlas is, why Allah accepts only sincere deeds, and how to build it

questions.q: Explain the hijrah example in the hadith on intentions. (4 marks, our own question)
questions.a: The same journey is worship for one (for Allah and His Messenger) and worldly for another (for gain or marriage): the reward follows the intention.
questions.model: Point: the same action can differ in reward. Evidence: the hijrah example (Bukhari and Muslim). Explain: both travelled to Madinah, but only the one who went for Allah got the reward of hijrah.

questions.q: Allah looks at your hearts and ...

Write a reflection in the portal response box: choose three deeds you do every week; for each, write the best intention to have and how you will check your heart. Start: 'When I ..., my intention is ...'
questions.a: Three deeds with sincere intentions and a self-check, linked to the hadith
questions.model: Teacher writes: 'When I help with the washing up, my intention is to please Allah and serve my parents. I check by doing it even when no one thanks me.'

questions.q: why is ikhlas called the hardest thing for the soul?
questions.a: The nafs loves praise; it takes constant effort

questions.q: Back to our ponder: can two people get different reward for the same deed?
